description.p: GMNB (GlazeMyNumbers,Baby) is a Rust port of the open-source Windows Calculator with a GTK 4 interface that is considerably prettier than it needs to be. The original arbitrary-precision engine was ported function-for-function and is verified against the real C++ engine.

ul.li: Standard, Scientific and Programmer calculators with history and memory
Graphing with variables, tracing and function analysis
Date calculation and unit conversion for 13 categories, including live currency rates
Seven colour palettes in light and dark — including one that follows your desktop's accent colour and one you design yourself — and a background that blooms when you type

description.p: On x86-64 PCs GMNB needs a CPU with AVX2 (x86-64-v3): Intel Core from Haswell (2013) or AMD from Excavator (2015) on, though not every Pentium, Celeron or Atom. Its lean twin, DGMNB, runs on any 64-bit PC.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by Microsoft. Based on microsoft/calculator (MIT).

screenshot.caption: Graphing: four equations, a variable slider and an inequality

description.p: GMNB gets a lean twin, DGMNB, built from the same shared core.

ul.li: Function analysis shows only what is proven: every row comes from a certified analysis, and a row it can't prove says so instead of guessing
Exact answers such as √2, π/2 + kπ and −9/4 wherever exact arithmetic confirms them
Settings → Window: a background opacity slider for a see-through window, and a switch to turn off Vulkan acceleration (from the next launch) to save memory
On x86-64, built for CPUs with AVX2; on any other, a small launcher explains why instead of crashing
Function analysis and heavy graphs no longer block the window
Hostile or huge graph input is rejected instead of crashing
Generated and built-in palettes keep text readable
Screen readers hear the 2nd/inverse/hyperbolic key names and toggle states
Manual currency refresh works even when the network monitor says offline

description.p: First release: every Windows Calculator mode, ported to Rust.
